name: max_flow_min_cut
author: 991d1029
description: Computes the maximum flow between a source and a sink node with the Edmonds-Karp algorithm, and the matching minimum cut (the bottleneck edges whose removal separates source from sink). Use for questions like 'how much can flow from A to B?', 'where is the bottleneck between A and B?', 'which edges must be removed to disconnect A from B?' or, with capacity='unit', 'how many edge-disjoint paths connect A and B?'. Works on directed graphs (arcs follow edge direction) and undirected graphs (each edge carries capacity both ways). By default each edge's capacity is its weight (unweighted graphs: 1); capacity can also be 'unit' or a numeric edge attribute such as 'airlines'. Returns the max flow value, the size of the source and sink sides of the cut, and up to top_k cut edges (largest capacity first, ties by node id) as from/to nodes with capacity. If the sink is unreachable the flow is 0. Source and sink must differ; use lookup_node to find node ids.

graph_id.description: Id of the graph to analyse.

source.description: Node id where the flow starts. Use lookup_node to find ids.

sink.description: Node id where the flow ends; must differ from source.

capacity.description: Edge capacity: 'weight' (default, edge weight), 'unit' (every edge 1), or the name of a numeric edge attribute such as 'airlines'.

top_k.description: Maximum number of cut edges to list.
